title: Amazon acquires key assets of AI startup Decart for reported $7.5B
author: Maria Deutscher
contentSnippet:
UPDATED 20:40 EST / NOVEMBER 23 2026

Amazon acquires key assets of AI startup Decart for reported $7.5B

Amazon.com Inc. today announced plans to hire the technical staff of startup Decart.AI Inc. and acquire its core technology.

The company didn’t disclose the terms of the deal. However, sources told Bloomberg that Amazon is paying about $7.5 billion. That’s nearly twice the valuation Decart reportedly received after its most recent funding round in May.

In August, reports emerged that the company had drawn takeover interest from Anthropic PBC. The artificial intelligence provider reportedly sought to buy Decart for $6 billion but walked away from the deal in September. Rumors that Amazon could swoop in emerged the following month.

Decart founders Dean Leitersdorf, Moshe Shalev and Orian Leitersdorf will join the tech giant along with Decart’s research team. Additionally, Amazon is acquiring the technology behind the company’s DOS platform, which helps boost the efficiency of AI models. Decart claims that the software can reduce the cost of some neural networks by a hundredfold.

The company hasn’t shared detailed information about how DOS works. However, the blog post in which Decart announced its May funding round did reveal that the platform optimizes AI models by “tuning the kernels.”

Kernels are the basic building blocks of neural networks. They’re relatively simple code snippets designed to run across a large number of chip cores. One common approach to optimizing them, kernel fusion, combines multiple kernels into a single code snippet that uses less hardware. In July, Decart disclosed that a custom model it had developed with DOS uses kernel fusion.

The company says that the platform also includes “proprietary compilers.” AI compilers translate neural networks into the platform-specific programming language of the host chip. They also optimize the models along they way. For example, the compiler that Amazon Web Services offers for its AWS Trainium machine learning chip uses quantization to compress models into a more memory-efficient form.

It’s unclear whether Decart positions DOS as an alternative to the default compilers provided with AI accelerators. According to Amazon, Decart has “worked closely” with its engineers since 2025 to optimize the performance of workloads deployed on its Trainium chips. The newest commercially available iterat

summary.tldr:
Amazon has announced the acquisition of key assets and the technical team from AI startup Decart.AI Inc. for a reported $7.5 billion. The deal includes the hiring of Decart founders Dean Leitersdorf, Moshe Shalev, and Orian Leitersdorf, alongside their research staff. While Amazon did not officially confirm the financial terms, the reported figure represents nearly double the valuation Decart achieved during its May funding round. Anthropic PBC had previously engaged in acquisition talks with Decart for $6 billion before withdrawing in September.

The core of the acquisition is Decart’s 'DOS' platform, a software suite designed to optimize AI model efficiency through kernel tuning and proprietary compilers. Decart claims the platform can reduce neural network costs by up to 100x. The technology utilizes techniques such as kernel fusion—combining multiple neural network code snippets to reduce hardware overhead—and specialized compilers that translate models for specific chip architectures. Amazon intends to integrate this technology to enhance the performance and cost-efficiency of its custom silicon, specifically the AWS Trainium3 chips, which currently deliver 2.52 petaflops of FP8 performance.

Notably, the acquisition excludes Decart’s internally developed AI models, such as the 'Lucy 2.5' and 'Oasis 3' world models, which are designed for low-latency content generation and robotic training data, respectively. Amazon’s integration efforts will focus on optimizing both inference and training workloads, building upon a collaborative relationship between Decart and AWS engineers that began in 2025.
takeaways: **Acquisition Value:** Amazon is reportedly paying $7.5 billion for Decart’s assets and talent, significantly higher than the startup's previous valuation.
**Core Technology:** The 'DOS' platform optimizes AI models via kernel fusion and proprietary compilers, with claims of reducing neural network costs by up to 100x.
**Hardware Integration:** The technology will be applied to AWS Trainium3 chips, which are rated at 2.52 petaflops for FP8 data processing.
**Excluded Assets:** The deal does not include Decart’s proprietary AI models, specifically the Lucy 2.5 and Oasis 3 world models.
**Previous Interest:** Anthropic PBC reportedly attempted to acquire Decart for $6 billion in August before walking away from negotiations in September.

title: Anthropic’s Claude Ship automates the final stage of the software development pipeline
author: Mike Wheatley
contentSnippet:
UPDATED 20:30 EST / NOVEMBER 23 2026

Anthropic’s Claude Ship automates the final stage of the software development pipeline

Anthropic PBC isn’t satisfied with having Claude just write new software. With a new update today, Claude now can tell developers when the code it has generated is ready to ship into production environments.

The company announced the launch of Claude Ship , which is a new suite of artificial intelligence agents capable of automating code reviews, bug fixes and approvals. The last one is the most interesting of those capabilities, because code reviews and fixes are nothing new for AI . But Claude’s ability to automatically approve code changes based on the policies predetermined by an organization’s developer team is a novel development that has not been seen before.

Claude Ship is an effort by Anthropic to eliminate the new bottleneck that has emerged in the code review and approval process at companies that have already adopted AI code generation tools. At those organizations, fresh code is being whipped up in double-quick time, and there are also AI agents for checking that code and providing fixes if it’s not working as hoped. But until now, the final review and approval process has always been performed by humans. Claude Ship changes that.

The idea is that human developers can delegate final approval authority to Claude, so now all they really have to do is determine the quality and security standards of the code they’re asking AI to create.

“Most teams want a person to approve every change and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line,” Anthropic said in a blog post. “But a lot of developers build with agents now. On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code and we wanted everything after the pull request to move that fast too.”

Anthropic said Claude Ship consists of three parts. The first is Code Review, which is a tool that has been generally available for some time already. The other two are PR Steward and Claude Approvals, and they’re both still in beta.

PR Steward is designed to handle issues such as failing continuous integration checks, merge conflicts and feedback from Code Review. After each push, it will leave comments on what changes were made and how to roll them back if necessary.

Once PR Steward is done, Claude Approvals takes over. It works by applying an approval policy that’s left

summary.tldr:
Anthropic has launched Claude Ship, a suite of AI agents designed to automate the final stages of the software development lifecycle, specifically code reviews, bug fixes, and production approvals. By allowing developers to delegate final approval authority to Claude based on organization-defined policies, the tool aims to remove the bottleneck created by human-in-the-loop requirements in high-velocity AI-assisted coding environments. The system is intended to accelerate the transition from pull request to production by automating tasks that previously required manual oversight.

Claude Ship consists of three distinct components: the existing Code Review tool, and two new beta features, PR Steward and Claude Approvals. PR Steward manages continuous integration failures, merge conflicts, and feedback implementation, while Claude Approvals executes final sign-offs based on natural language policies stored within the codebase repository. Anthropic recommends that early adopters initially deploy Claude Approvals in an 'observe-only' mode and limit usage to single repositories to mitigate risks associated with automated production deployments.
takeaways: **Component Architecture:** Claude Ship comprises three modules: Code Review (generally available), PR Steward (beta), and Claude Approvals (beta).
**Approval Mechanism:** Claude Approvals functions by reading approval policies defined in natural language files stored directly within the codebase repository.
**Compatibility:** The suite is currently available to Claude Team and Enterprise subscribers and supports integration with GitHub repositories.
**Risk Mitigation:** Anthropic advises users to implement 'observe-only' mode for the beta-stage Claude Approvals and to set monthly spending limits during initial deployment.

title: Anthropic Launches Claude Ship for GitHub Pull Request Review and Fixes
author: Asif Razzaq
contentSnippet: Anthropic just released Claude Ship Claude Ship is a set of Anthropic agents that takes GitHub pull requests from review to approval. It bundles 3 agents: Code Review , PR Steward and Claude Approvals . Your GitHub branch rules still decide what merges. TL;DR Size: 3 agents with a local /ship command. Runs on: Anthropic’s cloud for Code Review and PR Steward. /ship runs in the Claude Code CLI locally. Performance: Most Code Reviews finish in 6 to 10 minutes, about 3x faster than the research preview. Best: Claude Code team merged PRs more than doubled from June to September (self-reported). What is Claude Ship? Per the Claude Ship docs , each agent owns 1 step: Code Review looks for logic errors, security vulnerabilities and broken edge cases. Findings land as inline comments, ranked by severity. PR Steward works on failing checks, merge conflicts and review comments. It pushes commits with its fixes. Claude Approvals checks each PR against an approval policy your team writes. Code Review is generally available . The other 2 are in public beta. How does Claude Ship work on a pull request? Code Review finds problems. PR Steward pushes fixes, and a fix can start another review. Claude Approvals then applies your policy. The merge follows your GitHub branch rules. PR Steward is designed not to approve or merge. After each push, it comments on its changes and how to undo them. Developers steer it with @claude and stop it with @claude stop . Claude Approvals reads a policy file at .claude/approvals.yml . Anthropic calls it a smarter CODEOWNERS file. A rule can require 2 people on billing code and 1 on test fixtures. Rules can read PR facts and classifier answers, but not CI results. What does /ship do for developers? Developers run /ship in Claude Code. It commits, pushes and opens the PR. Claude reviews it, then ‘watches’ feedback and failing checks. You merge yourself. Requirements are Claude Code v2.1.330 or later, GitHub CLI 2.63 or later, and git 2.38 or later. A watch ends after 7 days, or on merge or close. /steward skips the review on an open PR. When Claude acts alone, Claude Code blocks merge, approve, auto-merge and force-push commands. Still, a watch uses your own gh and git sign-ins. Claude Ship benchmarks: what has Anthropic reported? Anthropic has published no public benchmark. It shares internal results from its launch post and engineering blog :

summary.tldr:
Anthropic has launched Claude Ship, a suite of three specialized agents designed to automate the GitHub pull request lifecycle from initial review to final approval. The system consists of Code Review, which identifies logic errors and security vulnerabilities; PR Steward, which resolves merge conflicts and failing checks by pushing commits; and Claude Approvals, which enforces custom team policies defined in a .claude/approvals.yml file. The tool integrates with the Claude Code CLI, allowing developers to initiate the workflow via a local /ship command.

Performance metrics reported by Anthropic indicate that code reviews typically complete within 6 to 10 minutes, representing a 3x speed improvement over the initial research preview. The system is designed to respect existing GitHub branch protection rules, with PR Steward explicitly restricted from approving or merging code. While Code Review is currently generally available, PR Steward and Claude Approvals remain in public beta. Deployment requires Claude Code v2.1.330, GitHub CLI 2.63, and git 2.38 or later, with the system utilizing the user's local git and GitHub credentials for all operations.
takeaways: **Agent Architecture:** The suite comprises three distinct agents: Code Review (vulnerabilities/logic), PR Steward (fixes/conflicts), and Claude Approvals (policy enforcement).

**Policy Configuration:** Claude Approvals uses a .claude/approvals.yml file, described as a smarter alternative to CODEOWNERS, allowing for granular rules like requiring two reviewers for specific billing-related code.
**CLI Integration:** The /ship command in Claude Code automates the commit, push, and PR opening process, while /steward allows for manual intervention on existing open pull requests.
**Safety Constraints:** When operating autonomously, Claude Code blocks sensitive commands including merge, approve, auto-merge, and force-push to ensure human oversight.
**Performance:** Internal engineering data shows review times of 6 to 10 minutes, with the Claude Code team reporting a doubling of merged PRs between June and September.

title: AI agent provider Sierra closes $1.75B investment amid rapid revenue growth
author: Maria Deutscher
contentSnippet:
UPDATED 18:49 EST / NOVEMBER 23 2026

AI agent provider Sierra closes $1.75B investment amid rapid revenue growth

Six months after its last funding round , artificial intelligence startup Sierra Technologies Inc. today announced that it has closed a $1.75 billion late-stage investment.

Greenoaks and Lightspeed led the Series F deal. They were joined by a group of returning backers that included Alphabet Inc.’s GV fund.

Sierra sells a set of cloud services that enables workers to create AI agents without writing code. The centerpiece of the suite is Ghostwriter, which can automatically generate agents based on user-provided prompts and files. A software team, for example, could upload a set of bug reports and request an agent that can automatically group them by problem type.

Ghostwriter checks the dataset that users upload for formatting errors before putting it to use. Once an agent is ready, the tool simulates user conversations to find potential bugs. Ghostwriter places particular emphasis on edge cases, unusual requests that can trip up an agent if they’re not addressed during development.

Sierra also offers a second development tool called Horizon. It can be used to create agents that automate time-consuming tasks. A marketing team could build an agent that monitors user interactions with a product page over several months, finds areas for improvement and automatically makes the necessary optimizations.

Sierra powers customers’ agents using more than a dozen large language models. Simple requests are sent to latency-optimized LLMs, while more complex queries are processed by pricier frontier models. Sierra says that it also uses several internally developed algorithms.

Customers can manage their AI projects using a third Sierra product called Agent Studio. According to the company, it includes over 40 connectors that enable agents to retrieve information from external systems. There’s also a tool for building custom connectors.

Agent Studio detects gaps in agents’ knowledge. Furthermore, it can automatically fix some of those gaps. The platform detects when a human support representative answers a customer inquiry that the help desk hasn’t encountered before and turns it into a knowledge base article. From there, agents can use the article to answer similar requests.

The studio also lends itself to certain other tasks. A collaboration feature e

summary.tldr:
AI agent provider Sierra Technologies Inc. has closed a $1.75 billion late-stage Series F investment round led by Greenoaks and Lightspeed, with participation from returning backers including Alphabet Inc.’s GV fund. The round marks Sierra's third funding raise in 14 months and follows the company's annualized revenue surpassing $400 million, half of which was added in the preceding quarter. Sierra's enterprise customer base currently includes half of the Fortune 50, and the fresh capital will be deployed to expand its product portfolio and scale its sales organization.

Sierra provides a no-code cloud suite for building and managing enterprise AI agents. Its core development tool, Ghostwriter, generates agents from user-provided prompts and files, validates dataset formatting, and simulates user conversations to stress-test edge cases. A secondary tool, Horizon, builds agents for continuous workflow automation like marketing product page optimization. The platform orchestrates agent requests across more than a dozen large language models—routing simple queries to latency-optimized models and complex tasks to frontier models—alongside proprietary algorithms developed internally.

Management and integrations are handled via Agent Studio, which features over 40 pre-built external connectors, a custom connector builder, multi-person team collaboration reviews, and step-by-step workflow debugging tools. Agent Studio also features automated knowledge-gap remediation that converts novel human support responses into knowledge base articles, while an auxiliary assistant named Explorer proactively flags business events and searches internal corporate datasets.
takeaways: **Funding Details:** Sierra closed a $1.75 billion Series F funding round led by Greenoaks and Lightspeed, with participation from Alphabet Inc.'s GV fund, representing its third raise in 14 months.
**Financial & Market Metrics:** Sierra's annualized revenue recently topped $400 million, adding nearly half that total in a single quarter, and its customer base covers half of the Fortune 50.
**Core Development Tools:** The company's platform includes Ghostwriter for prompt-based agent generation and edge-case simulation, and Horizon for automating time-consuming operational tasks.

**Model Routing & Architecture:** Sierra powers customer agents using a mix of more than a dozen large language models (routing simple tasks to latency-optimized models and complex queries to frontier models) plus internal proprietary algorithms.

**Management Infrastructure:** Agent Studio provides over 40 external system connectors, custom connector creation, multi-user review workflows, granular step-by-step debugging, and automated knowledge-gap resolution from human support tickets.

title: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer
author: Simon Willison AI
contentSnippet: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer GLM 5.4 is now available from Chinese AI lab Z.ai. It's their first model to use a looped transformer architecture, which they describe like this: In a standard Transformer, each layer runs once per forward pass. In a Loop Transformer, a group of weight-shared layers runs for multiple iterations, refining the hidden states from the previous pass. This gives us a deeper network without increasing the parameter count. This is the second mention of looped transformers I've seen in the past week - the first was Inkling 2 Mini from Thinking Machines Lab on November 20th, who said: Inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer, running the middle layers of the model three times for every token. This allows the model to apply more reasoning and reach the right answer with fewer tokens, especially on tasks such as agentic coding that depend on reasoning quality. GLM 5.4 is not (yet?) available as open weights. I tried it out using the Z.ai API, for which I had to sign up for their Coding Plan subscription because 5.4 cannot currently be accessed through the regular API. It turns out both coding plan and regular API share the same OpenAI-compatible Responses API (at https://api.z.ai/api/v1 ), and the API key for the coding plan worked with that and gave me access to the new model. I built a llm-glm plugin , then realized that llm-zai by Tommy Hughes already exists! I've shipped mine purely because llm-zai doesn't yet support the new model, but I'll likely retire mine once that plugin catches up. Here are pelicans for GLM-5.4 on low, high, and max. This is the max one: I realized I never ran pelicans for GLM-5.3, so here those are for the same effort levels. They look similar in quality to 5.4. It's interesting how GLM 5.1 and GLM 5.2 produced radically different pelicans from other models. The pelicans for 5.3 and 5.4 are much more comparable to those I get from OpenAI or Anthropic models - the previous generations had their own distinctive look. I made a comparison grid showing the four generations of GLM pelicans all in one place. The style transition between 5.2 and 5.3 is pretty stark. Tags: ai , generative-ai , llms , llm , pelican-riding-a-bicycle , llm-release , ai-in-china , glm

summary.tldr:
Chinese AI lab Z.ai has released GLM-5.4, a model utilizing a novel 'looped transformer' architecture. Unlike standard transformers where each layer executes once per forward pass, the looped architecture employs a group of weight-shared layers that iterate multiple times to refine hidden states. This design allows for increased effective network depth without expanding the total parameter count, a strategy recently mirrored by Thinking Machines Lab’s Inkling 2 Mini, which runs middle layers three times per token to enhance reasoning capabilities for agentic coding tasks.

GLM-5.4 is currently not available as open weights and is restricted to users subscribed to Z.ai’s 'Coding Plan.' The model is accessible via an OpenAI-compatible API at https://api.z.ai/api/v1. While existing tools like Tommy Hughes’s 'llm-zai' plugin provide access to previous Z.ai models, they do not yet support GLM-5.4, necessitating the development of new integration plugins. Visual benchmarks, specifically the 'pelican-riding-a-bicycle' prompt, indicate that GLM-5.4 produces outputs more stylistically aligned with OpenAI and Anthropic models than the distinct, idiosyncratic visual styles observed in GLM-5.1 and GLM-5.2.
takeaways: **Architecture:** GLM-5.4 uses a looped transformer design where weight-shared layers iterate to refine hidden states, increasing depth without increasing parameter count.
**Availability:** The model is closed-weights and requires a specific 'Coding Plan' subscription to access via the Z.ai OpenAI-compatible API.
**Industry Context:** The looped transformer approach is gaining traction, with Thinking Machines Lab’s Inkling 2 Mini also utilizing a similar mechanism to improve reasoning in agentic coding.

**Visual Benchmarking:** Qualitative testing via 'pelican-riding-a-bicycle' prompts shows a shift in GLM-5.4 toward visual styles comparable to Western frontier models, marking a departure from the unique aesthetic of GLM-5.1 and 5.2.

title: Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang
author: Lauren Feiner
contentSnippet: After Nvidia’s board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Appearing on Stephen A. Smith’s radio show shortly after the news came out, Trump said that Huang would “end up on his feet.” “You know the expression, anybody can be replaced,” Trump said, floating Apple’s ex-CEO Tim Cook as a potential CEO candidate. It didn’t take long for Trump to begin softening his approach, making it clear he’d welcome Huang back into the role of CEO even if Nvidia’s own board wasn’t ready to do so. Behind the scenes, the Trump administration was working to grease the landing for Huang’s return. And soon, Nvidia’s board changed its tune: Barely a week after insisting they all agreed to shut the door on Huang’s return, they voted unanimously to reinstate him as CEO, president, and board director. “There’s nothing wrong with a comeback,” Trump said in a celebratory call to CNBC. Trump then posted an image on Truth Social of Huang transposed onto Trump’s own body in the infamous photo of him raising his fist after being shot at a campaign rally. In his raised fist, Huang-on-Trump’s-body is clutching a scarlet bra, holding it high in the air. Even after a decisive blow to the president’s power as Democrats swept the midterm elections, Trump appears to maintain his position as a corporate kingmaker. Trump said he spoke with Huang the night prior to his reinstatement and had been in communication with the board both “directly and indirectly.” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement that “President Trump was totally involved” in the board’s decision — Trump decided near the end of last week that he wanted to lead efforts to get Huang reappointed, per The New York Times, so he asked Vice President JD Vance to act as a liaison between Huang and Nvidia’s board, providing reassurances that the move wouldn’t pose a security risk. Trump also reportedly dialed into Nvidia’s Sunday night board meeting to make the case for his return. “I made the deal,” he told CNBC on Monday. News of Huang’s reappointment, nearly as dramatic as Sam Altman’s return to his CEO role after being voted out by OpenAI’s board in 2023, was a widespread shock to experts, analysts, and investors, particularly after Nvidia’s board had assured sta

summary.tldr:
Nvidia’s board has unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, president, and board director just one week after announcing his departure. The reversal followed intense intervention by President Donald Trump, who personally lobbied the board and utilized Vice President JD Vance as a liaison to provide assurances regarding national security concerns. The initial resignation was prompted by revelations of an affair between Huang and Alice Huang, a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed, who has been linked by U.S. intelligence to Chinese state espionage. Huang also faced allegations of additional affairs with company employees and accusations of misleading the board regarding his conduct.

To facilitate the return, Nvidia’s board established a new National Security and Export Control Committee composed of independent directors and announced the creation of a chief compliance officer role. Despite these measures, the reinstatement has triggered significant political backlash. Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer and Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries have pledged aggressive congressional investigations into both Nvidia’s export control compliance and the Trump administration’s involvement in the board’s decision-making process. The SEC is also reportedly investigating whether Nvidia misled investors during the period surrounding the initial resignation and subsequent reinstatement.
takeaways: **Reinstatement Details:** Jensen Huang was restored to his roles as CEO, president, and board director following a unanimous board vote and direct intervention by President Trump, who reportedly dialed into a Sunday night board meeting.

**Espionage Allegations:** Reports indicate Alice Huang, with whom Jensen Huang had an affair, maintained contact with a Chinese intelligence agency for over a year; her business partner, Kang Wei, is also alleged to have ties to the same agency.
**Governance Changes:** Nvidia is creating a new C-suite position, chief compliance officer, and has formed a National Security and Export Control Committee to oversee trade compliance.

**Congressional Oversight:** Democratic leadership, including Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries, has announced plans to investigate the Trump administration's role in the reinstatement and Nvidia's adherence to U.S. chip export controls.
**Market Impact:** The announcement of Huang's return caused extreme volatility, triggering a circuit-breaker halt in NASDAQ-100 futures trading on Monday morning.

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is back. What happens next?
author: Richard Lawler
contentSnippet: After the leather-jacketed CEO, president, and co-founder of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, acknowledged an affair with Megaspeed exec Alice Huang, his company initially announced an investigation. However, after The New York Times reported there was evidence of another affair, this time with an Nvidia executive who reported directly to him, a board meeting that night ended with Huang’s resignation , and Nvidia CFO Colette Kress was installed as the new interim CEO. And then… Huang was back. In recent years, Nvidia has become a key part of the Trump administration’s AI push, a central figure in negotiations over potential Chinese access to cutting-edge AI hardware, and a company that has used its now $4 trillion-plus market cap to finance other AI companies. Saying it received input “from senior levels of the United States government,” Nvidia’s board announced his return as CEO on November 23rd, less than two weeks after his resignation. summary.tldr:
Nvidia co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang has returned to his position as of November 23rd, less than two weeks after resigning following reports of affairs with a Megaspeed executive and a direct report. The board reinstated Huang after receiving input from senior levels of the United States government, with the Trump administration actively involved in the process. During his brief absence, Nvidia CFO Colette Kress served as interim CEO, and Arm CEO Rene Haas was reportedly considered for the role before declining.

Nvidia currently holds a market capitalization exceeding $4 trillion and generates over $200 billion in annual profit. Despite the leadership transition, the company faces significant regulatory and financial scrutiny; Nvidia’s stock closed down 14% following the news, and the SEC is investigating the company’s accounting practices. Additionally, the California Attorney General has issued a subpoena to the firm. Recent disclosures indicate the Trump administration approved the sale of over 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies, highlighting Nvidia's central role in current U.S. geopolitical and AI hardware policy.
takeaways: **Leadership Timeline:** Jensen Huang resigned following reports of internal affairs and was reinstated as CEO on November 23rd after intervention from the U.S. government.
**Regulatory Scrutiny:** The SEC is investigating Nvidia’s accounting practices, and the California Attorney General has issued a subpoena to the company.
**Market Position:** Nvidia maintains a market capitalization of over $4 trillion and reports annual profits exceeding $200 billion.
**Export Policy:** The Trump administration authorized the sale of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese entities.
**Stock Performance:** Nvidia shares declined 14% over the week following the leadership instability and regulatory disclosures.

title: Welcome to elite impunity, Jensen Huang
author: Elizabeth Lopatto
contentSnippet: I suppose I must issue a hearty congratulations to Jensen Huang. Huang is CEO of Nvidia again, to the surprise of basically everyone except President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance, who made sure it happened. Now, those of us who had some kind of basic education on what a “free market” is might find it objectionable to have the American president strong-arming a major American company. But our billionaire tech overlords care about the “free market” exactly as much as they care about “free speech,” which is to say not at all. Watching Silicon Valley cheer for what is, effectively, a sign of a command economy has certainly been bracing. But then, why would they give a shit? Their only real beliefs are that they should remain rich and above the law. Jensen may not have exchanged emails with Jeffrey Epstein, but he’s squarely at the Epstein table now. I have argued here, in the past, that the Epstein case laid bare the real politics of the revanchist American right wing: total elite impunity. Well, here it is again! If you are close enough with Trump, it doesn’t matter if you may have jeopardized national security by fucking an alleged Chinese spy. You won’t even be investigated for it before the American president calls in to your board of directors’ meeting to demand you be reinstated. I mean, it is the era of gangster tech regulation — what were any of us expecting? The deal was reportedly brokered by Peter Thiel’s very own boy, Vance. Just so we can be absolutely clear about what transpired at Nvidia, let’s quickly go through the facts as we know them. A Chinese citizen named Alice Huang acquired the company she renamed Megaspeed, the Singaporean data firm at the center of this inquiry, in 2023. At some point, Huang met Huang, and the two were seen together at a dinner that December. From 2024 to 2025, Megaspeed received more than 200 Nvidia shipments. summary.tldr:
Jensen Huang has been reinstated as CEO of Nvidia, just days after his November 12, 2026, resignation following reports of professional misconduct and national security concerns. The reversal occurred on November 23, 2026, despite the company's board chair stating on November 17 that there was no intention to reinstate him. The reinstatement followed a pressure campaign from high-profile tech executives—including Elon Musk, Tim Sweeney, Travis Kalanick, and Bill Ackman—and direct intervention from President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance, who reportedly brokered the deal.

The controversy centers on allegations that Huang engaged in an affair with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen who acquired the data firm Megaspeed in 2023. Megaspeed reportedly received over 200 Nvidia shipments between 2024 and 2025, leading to a U.S. government investigation into potential chip export control violations. Reports also surfaced regarding Huang’s affairs with Nvidia employees and allegations of workplace intimidation. Despite these findings, President Trump publicly stated on CNBC that he provided the board with assurances that Huang is "absolutely fine," effectively shielding the executive from the consequences typically associated with such conflicts of interest.
takeaways: **Timeline of Events:** Jensen Huang resigned on November 12, 2026, and was reinstated on November 23, 2026, following a board intervention influenced by the Trump administration.

**National Security Allegations:** The U.S. government began investigating Megaspeed, a firm linked to an alleged Chinese intelligence asset, for potential violations of chip export controls in September 2025.
**Corporate Misconduct:** Beyond the alleged relationship with Alice Huang, reports surfaced regarding Huang's affairs with Nvidia employees and claims of workplace abuse.
**Independent Investigation:** Nvidia’s board has appointed Joon Kim, a partner at Wachtell Lipton and former federal prosecutor, to conduct an investigation into the misconduct allegations.
**Political Context:** President Trump publicly claimed credit for protecting both Jensen Huang and Elon Musk from potential legal or professional consequences during his tenure.

title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes
author: Sarah Perez
contentSnippet:
Anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship. On Monday, the newly public AI company announced the launch of Claude Ship , a suite of AI agents for automating code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes.

The latter is the more interesting part of this new set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now. What’s notable about Claude Ship is not just that it can review proposed code changes and identify and address problems, but that it also includes an agent that can approve code changes automatically based on policies set by a development team.

The launch arrives at a time when AI coding agents have become increasingly capable of generating substantial amounts of code, leading to bottlenecks in reviewing and approving the code changes before they go live. With Claude Ship, the idea is to automate even more of the work involved in the development process, essentially by delegating approval authority to an AI agent itself.

“Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” a company blog post explains. “On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code, and we wanted everything after the PR to move that fast too.”

Claude Ship is launching in beta, allowing early adopters to use it to review pull requests (PRs), and then decide what’s ready to merge.

The new offering consists of Code Review, which is already generally available , and two new agents now in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. PR Steward focuses on addressing issues such as failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and feedback from Code Review. It also comments after every push on what it changed and how to roll it back, if needed.

Claude Approvals then applies an approval policy that the team writes as a file in the repository. This approval process can incorporate various signals, including Code Review findings or the company’s own classifiers, with policies written in natural language.

Because the offering is still in beta, Anthropic suggests running the approval functionality in observe-only mode first. Teams can also choose to start with just one repository and set monthly spending limits to have more control over the process.

Anthropic says teams will also stil

summary.tldr:
Anthropic has launched Claude Ship, a suite of AI agents designed to automate the code review, remediation, and approval lifecycle for software development teams. The toolset aims to resolve bottlenecks created by AI-generated code by delegating approval authority to an agent based on team-defined policies. Claude Ship is currently available to Claude Team and Enterprise plan users for GitHub repositories.

The suite comprises three components: Code Review (generally available), and two beta-stage agents, PR Steward and Claude Approvals. PR Steward manages CI check failures, merge conflicts, and feedback integration, while providing documentation on changes and rollback procedures. Claude Approvals allows teams to define custom approval policies via a repository-based file, utilizing natural language instructions and internal classifiers to determine if a pull request is ready for merge. Users can configure review depth (Quick, Standard, or Deep) and specify which changes require human intervention.

Anthropic recommends that teams initially deploy the approval functionality in an 'observe-only' mode to validate policy efficacy. The system allows for granular control, including setting monthly spending limits and restricting deployment to specific repositories. This release follows the company's internal use of Claude to manage its own codebase, aiming to accelerate the post-pull request development workflow.
takeaways: **Suite Components:** Claude Ship includes Code Review (GA), PR Steward (Beta), and Claude Approvals (Beta).
**Policy Configuration:** Approval logic is defined by teams in a repository-based file using natural language, incorporating signals from Code Review and custom classifiers.
**Operational Control:** Users can select between Quick, Standard, and Deep review settings and define specific criteria for human escalation.
**Deployment Scope:** The tools are currently available for GitHub repositories exclusively for users on Claude Team and Enterprise plans.
**Safety Features:** Anthropic advises an 'observe-only' phase for the approval agent and provides mechanisms for setting monthly spending limits.

title: Supertake raises $20M to let AI agents turn your market predictions into stock portfolios
author: Sarah Perez
contentSnippet:
AI investing startup Supertake has an interesting premise: What if your “takes” on the market could make you money without you having to pick stocks yourself? The service lets people turn their ideas into real investment portfolios, using frontier AI models and trading agents.

Now, the company has raised $20 million in seed funding to grow its business. The round was led by venture firm Adjacent (Nico Wittenborn), with participation from Coinbase Ventures and Union Square Ventures (USV). Numerous angel investors also joined, including Nat Friedman , who’s currently head of product at Meta Superintelligence Labs; Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch; renowned product manager Nikita Bier; investor Scott Belsky; and Nemil Dalal, a former Coinbase exec who is now a visiting partner at Y Combinator.

Michael Mignano originally incubated the startup at USV. He is the co-founder and former CEO of the podcasting platform Anchor, which Spotify acquired in 2019 for over $150 million. After leading Spotify’s podcasting business as “Head of Talk” for a few years, he joined the team at Lightspeed as a venture partner, betting on AI companies like Suno and Granola. He also co-founded Oboe, an AI education startup, and joined USV as a general partner in April.

“We really believed there was an opportunity to make investing more democratized…and give everyone and anyone the ability to invest in their own insights and beliefs and ideas,” Mignano said. While he will continue in his role as founder and executive chairman, he’s now brought in a team to run the company day to day.

summary.tldr:
Supertake, an AI-driven fintech startup, has raised $20 million in seed funding to develop a platform that translates natural language market predictions into automated stock portfolios. The round was led by Adjacent, with participation from Coinbase Ventures, Union Square Ventures (USV), and notable angel investors including Nat Friedman, Guillermo Rauch, and Nikita Bier. The company was incubated at USV by Michael Mignano, co-founder of Anchor, and is now led by CEO Lincoln Murr and CTO John Peterson, both formerly of Coinbase, where they led initiatives in agentic finance and AI product development.

The platform functions by allowing users to articulate investment theses in natural language, which the company’s proprietary software and frontier AI models then convert into actionable portfolios. Currently integrated with Coinbase and Robinhood, the service features a leaderboard where users can share and copy investment "takes." To mitigate risks associated with autonomous financial agents, Supertake employs guardrails including trade size limits, asset allow/deny lists, drift management, and a strict separation of duties that prevents agents from accessing brokerage credentials or executing withdrawals without explicit user consent. While currently focused on medium-to-long-term stock holdings, the team plans to expand into derivatives, shorts, and prediction market integrations.

Supertake is currently in a waitlisted beta phase. The founders report significant "skin in the game," with Mignano disclosing that the platform manages "hundreds of thousands" of his own capital, while Murr and Peterson have invested "tens of thousands" and "thousands," respectively. The new capital will be used to scale the engineering and design teams as the company seeks to evolve the traditional robo-advisor model into an agentic, intent-based investment experience.
takeaways: **Funding Details:** The $20 million seed round follows a previous $2 million pre-seed round, bringing total disclosed funding to $22 million.
**Leadership Background:** CEO Lincoln Murr and CTO John Peterson previously led AI product and engineering at Coinbase, specifically working on agentic wallets and advisor tools.
**Security Architecture:** The platform enforces strict isolation where AI agents cannot access brokerage credentials, withdraw funds, or trade outside of user-defined allow/deny lists.

**Platform Integration:** Supertake currently supports brokerage connectivity via Coinbase and Robinhood, with plans to expand to additional brokerages and asset classes like derivatives and perpetuals.

**Operational Model:** The company operates as a hybrid team based in New York and Austin, with Michael Mignano serving as founder and executive chairman while the co-founders manage daily operations.

title: Elon Musk and others rejoice as Jensen Huang is reinstated at Nvidia amid scandal
author: Amanda Silberling
contentSnippet:
A handful of tech CEOs, including Elon Musk, are celebrating Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia. Despite being caught in three affairs — including one with an alleged Chinese spy that has triggered multiple congressional investigations over national security concerns — Huang was reinstated as CEO and president of Nvidia on Monday morning.

“The mistake has been corrected,” Tesla and SpaceX leader Elon Musk wrote on X about Huang’s return.

The mistake has been corrected https://t.co/UKvEng9rCD

Musk had been among the most vocal tech leaders to advocate for Huang.

“I think it’s like kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak, and it just doesn’t seem like a good thing for shareholders,” Musk said last week at the DealBook Summit.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman had taken a more neutral stance, commenting last week, “It’s hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen.”

Altman had experienced a similar situation when he was ousted as CEO of OpenAI, then reinstated days later. After the announcement that Huang would return, Altman simply posted, “Jensen!” Many other tech CEOs have similarly refrained from commenting on the matter, given the shifting politics surrounding Huang’s ouster and reinstatement, as well as the national security concerns at the center of the controversy.

Jensen! — Sam Altman (@sama) November 23, 2026 In addition to Musk, Binance co-founder and former CEO Changpeng Zhao (CZ), who served prison time for failing to stop criminal activity on the Binance crypto exchange, is also supportive of Huang.

“Glad to see @JensenHuang back,” CZ posted on X with a clapping hands emoji.

Glad to see @JensenHuang back. 👏 https://t.co/WrUjvmEyVi

Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, who had been among 200,000 signatories on an open letter calling for Huang’s reinstatement, wrote on X, “Jensen’s return will be a demonstration of American resiliency to corporate, political and journalistic missteps.”

Another signatory on the open letter, former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick, who had similarly been driven out of the company he founded after scandals , also voiced his support for Huang on X.

Will have to save this for another day 😅😎 pic.twitter.com/dLqJosDpPZ

When Nvidia’s stock tanked in reaction to Huang’s ousting, billionaire hedge fund manager Bill Ackman said he believes that the Nvidia board was “not acting in the best interest of shareholders

summary.tldr:
Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO and president of Nvidia on Monday morning following a scandal involving three affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy that triggered congressional investigations over national security concerns. Tech leaders celebrated the move, with Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk writing on X that "the mistake has been corrected," comparing the initial ousting to kicking Michael Jordan off a winning team. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman posted "Jensen!" while Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick also voiced support. Sweeney was among 200,000 signatories on an open letter calling for Huang's reinstatement, and hedge fund manager Bill Ackman criticized Nvidia's board for failing fiduciary duties when the stock initially tanked.

Despite the tech industry celebration, elected officials expressed skepticism regarding national security implications. Senator John Cornyn (R-TX) questioned President Donald Trump's claims that the reinstatement poses no risk, while Senator Pete Ricketts (R-NB) stated that the decision does not excuse Huang from testifying or absolve Nvidia from answering for unaccounted-for chips. Huang remains scheduled to testify publicly before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3, as well as privately before three House committees.
takeaways: **Reinstatement Timeline:** Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO and president of Nvidia on Monday morning after a brief ousting sparked by personal scandals and an alleged Chinese spy investigation.

**Industry Support:** Elon Musk compared the ouster to kicking Michael Jordan off a winning team, while Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney participated in an open letter signed by 200,000 people demanding Huang's return.
**Congressional Scrutiny:** Senators John Cornyn and Pete Ricketts voiced sharp national security concerns regarding Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy and unaccounted-for chips.
**Upcoming Testimony:** Huang is scheduled to testify publicly before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3 and privately before three House committees.

title: Ladybird's first alpha release
author: Simon Willison AI
contentSnippet: Ladybird is an astonishingly ambitious project: a new browser, in 2026, with its own implementation of most of the key components - HTML parsing, CSS engine, layout, JavaScript, even WebAssembly. It still uses a few external components - things like HarfBuzz for text shaping, Skia for 2D graphics, ffmpeg for video, and SQLite for the things you do with SQLite. Everything else is part of Ladybird, or code brought in from Ladybird's even more ambitious predecessor project SerenityOS . This morning the Ladybird project released their first alpha , which means you can now install the browser (on macOS or Linux) without having to compile it yourself! I've been trying it out today, and it's very impressive. It feels fast, the UI is lightweight and intuitive, and most of the websites I've tried to load in it have worked as they should. It looks like this (showing my video-compressor tool): Here's the process tree after I opened six tabs in one window and another tab in a second window (generated by this script , thanks Claude): Ladybird (72925) [240 MB] └── Hub (72926) [61 MB] ├── RequestServer (72927) [29 MB] ├── ProcessReaper (72928) [1 MB] ├── Compositor (72930) [123 MB] ├── RequestServer (72953) [36 MB] ├── WebContent (72984) [819 MB] ├── MediaServer (73006) [118 MB] ├── VideoDecoderServer (73007) [20 MB] ├── WebContent (73052) [144 MB] ├── WebContent (73057) [73 MB] ├── WebContent (73073) [166 MB] ├── WebContent (73094) [70 MB] ├── WebContent (73112) [116 MB] ├── RequestServer (73113) [27 MB] └── WebContent (73185) [60 MB] Ladybird runs different tabs in different processes, an isolation mechanism used by most browsers (well, technically Chrome uses a process-per-site). I tried Ladybird against several of my more advanced tool examples - like the video-compressor shown above, which runs ffmpeg compiled to WebAssembly. I had it resize its own screenshot using my image-resize tool . It happily runs my Pyodide REPL (Python compiled to WebAssembly) too. The one thing I tried that didn't work was Datasette Lite , which runs Pyodide in a complicated arrangement of service workers and web workers. Attempting to start Datasette Lite displays this error: undefined is not a function (evaluated from 'navigator.serviceWorker.startMessages') I filed an issue about this , then found a FIXME annotation in the source code. The October explosion The project has been leaning he

summary.tldr:
The Ladybird browser project has released its first alpha, marking the transition from a source-only project to pre-compiled binaries available for macOS and Linux. Unlike most modern browsers that rely on Chromium or WebKit, Ladybird implements its own HTML parser, CSS engine, layout engine, JavaScript engine, and WebAssembly runtime. It maintains a hybrid architecture, utilizing specific external libraries for specialized tasks, including HarfBuzz for text shaping, Skia for 2D graphics, ffmpeg for video decoding, and SQLite for database operations.

The browser employs a multi-process architecture to ensure site isolation, similar to standard industry practices. Process tree analysis of a multi-tab session reveals distinct processes for the Hub, RequestServer, Compositor, MediaServer, and individual WebContent processes for each tab. During testing, the browser successfully executed complex WebAssembly-based tools, including video compression and Pyodide (Python compiled to WebAssembly). However, the alpha currently lacks support for certain advanced features, such as Service Workers, which caused a failure when attempting to run Datasette Lite.
takeaways: **Architecture:** Ladybird utilizes a multi-process model where each tab runs in its own WebContent process, isolated from the main Hub and auxiliary servers like MediaServer and RequestServer.
**External Dependencies:** The project integrates established libraries for non-core functions, specifically HarfBuzz (text), Skia (2D graphics), ffmpeg (video), and SQLite.
**Compatibility:** The browser successfully runs WebAssembly-heavy applications like Pyodide and custom video-compressor tools, but currently fails on sites requiring Service Worker support.
**Availability:** The first alpha release provides pre-compiled binaries for macOS and Linux, removing the previous requirement for users to compile the source code manually.

title: Google Search’s AI Mode can now tap into Drive and Wallet for more personalized responses
author: Aisha Malik
contentSnippet:
Google announced on Monday that it’s expanding Personal Intelligence in Search’s AI Mode with integrations for Google Drive, Google Wallet, and the Gemini app. Personal Intelligence is designed to offer users more personalized, context-aware answers by connecting to their Google apps and drawing on information from their digital lives. The feature can already connect to apps like Gmail, Google Calendar, and Google Photos.

By bringing Personal Intelligence in AI Mode to Drive, Wallet, and the Gemini app, Google is leveraging the wealth of user data that’s already within its ecosystem. Since users rely on these services, the tech giant can deliver more personalized experiences that rivals aren’t able to match. Of course, not everyone wants AI looking at their Wallet and Drive, so connecting the apps is optional, and you can turn Personal Intelligence on or off at any time.

Google says that connecting Google Wallet to Personal Intelligence lets users track their financial goals, cut everyday spending, and make better use of credit card rewards. The tech giant notes that if users choose to connect their Wallet, AI Mode can only read information from accounts and isn’t able to move or manage their money.

As for Drive, the company says important information related to a project or major decision is often scattered across documents and spreadsheets. By connecting Google Drive to Personal Intelligence, AI can draw on those files to provide more relevant, personalized answers, such as creating a tailored plan for tax season.

Users will also be able to share context between their Gemini app and AI Mode in Search, which means that if they explore an idea in the Gemini app, they won’t have to start over with AI Mode because it will already have the information, and vice versa.

Additionally, Google says users will soon be able to view the context that AI Mode uses via a new “Personalization” icon that will appear below responses.

The company also announced on Monday that users will start to see more personally relevant responses in AI Overviews and AI Mode that will be tailored to users’ recent search context.

title: Z AI Releases GLM-5.4: A 750B Loop Transformer That Runs 28 Layers Twice
author: Asif Razzaq
contentSnippet: Z.ai has released GLM-5.4 , its first flagship model built on a Loop Transformer architecture. The GLM-5.4 Loop Transformer runs 28 layers of the GLM-5 base model for 2 iterations. Z.ai says the model reaches intelligence comparable to 2T-3T parameter models. For developers, the pitch is ‘Generalized Coding’: code as the tool for video, games, 3D shaders and CAD. TL;DR Size: 750B-scale base. Active parameters not disclosed. Context window not officially listed (the blog discusses deployment at 1M context). Runs on: Z.ai-hosted only for now (GLM Coding Plan, ZCode, Z.ai Chat). Self-hosting hardware not disclosed until weights ship. Performance: No flagship benchmark table yet. Z.ai claims parity with 2T-3T parameter models. Best: +11.3 points on AIME25 (19.17 to 30.42) in Z.ai’s 30B looped ablation. Worst: +3.3 points on IFBench (50.20 to 53.47), the smallest gain. Z.ai also flags “marathon thinking” loops. What is GLM-5.4? GLM-5.4 is a 750B-scale Loop Transformer from Z.ai that runs shared layers twice per pass. It ships first inside Z.ai’s own products: the GLM Coding Plan , the ZCode desktop app and Z.ai Chat . Z.ai did not pre-train a looped model from scratch. It adapted the pre-trained GLM-5 base through continued training. The technical post states that looped models trained from scratch still trail unshared models at equal compute. Adapting an existing base raises the ceiling with a relatively small compute overhead. How does the Loop Transformer work? In a standard Transformer, each layer runs once per forward pass. In GLM-5.4, a group of 28 weight-shared layers runs for 2 iterations. Z.ai made 3 changes to keep this practical at 750B scale. Gated progressive updates Overwriting hidden states across loops made activation norms blow up. GLM-5.4 adds independent per-token gates for each iteration. The first pass writes small updates and builds global context. The second pass opens the gates to refine the output. On harder tokens, the first pass writes more aggressively. Hybrid KV cache A naive design keeps a full KV cache for every loop. GLM-5.4’s second loop reuses the sparse KV selected in pass 1. It keeps its own new KV only inside a local sliding window. So the extra loop costs 1 sliding window of KV cache, not a full context cache. Z.ai says this keeps the cost increase over GLM-5.3 under control at 1M context. Sparse attention index reuse The sec

summary.tldr:
Z.ai has unveiled GLM-5.4, a 750B-scale 'Loop Transformer' that achieves performance parity with 2T-3T parameter models by executing 28 shared layers twice per forward pass. Unlike models trained from scratch, GLM-5.4 was developed by applying continued training to the existing GLM-5 base, a strategy Z.ai claims overcomes the performance deficits typically seen in looped architectures. The model is currently available exclusively through Z.ai’s proprietary ecosystem, including the GLM Coding Plan, ZCode desktop application, and Z.ai Chat, with no immediate plans for self-hosting weights.

To manage the technical challenges of weight-sharing, Z.ai implemented three architectural modifications: gated progressive updates, which use per-token gates to prevent activation norm instability; a hybrid KV cache that reuses sparse KV data from the first pass while limiting the second pass to a local sliding window; and sparse attention index reuse. These optimizations allow the model to maintain a 1M context window without the memory overhead of a full second-pass cache. While formal benchmark tables are pending, Z.ai reports significant gains in internal ablations, including an 11.3-point increase on AIME25 and a 3.3-point improvement on IFBench.
takeaways: **Architecture:** GLM-5.4 utilizes a Loop Transformer design where 28 layers are executed twice, effectively scaling a 750B-parameter base to match the intelligence of 2T-3T parameter models.

**Training Methodology:** The model was created via continued training of the pre-trained GLM-5 base, as Z.ai found that looped models trained from scratch underperform compared to unshared models at equivalent compute levels.
**Memory Optimization:** The hybrid KV cache architecture prevents memory bloat at 1M context by reusing sparse KV data from the first loop and restricting the second loop to a local sliding window.
**Benchmark Performance:** Internal testing on a 30B looped ablation showed a 11.3-point gain on AIME25 (19.17 to 30.42) and a 3.3-point gain on IFBench (50.20 to 53.47).
**Deployment:** Access is currently restricted to Z.ai-hosted services, specifically the GLM Coding Plan, ZCode, and Z.ai Chat, with no public release of model weights.

author: Stevie Bonifield
contentSnippet: Nothing’s new AI device is the Ear Note, a set of earbuds and their microphone-equipped charging case that can record and transcribe conversations, with a connected app to manage the recordings, transcriptions and AI-generated summaries, similar to Apple’s new Watch feature and devices like Amazon’s Bee wearable. Earlier this year, Nothing introduced an Audio Snapshot recording feature in the Ear 3A. Anker’s Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro Max can also record directly to the earbuds’ case and generate AI transcripts and summaries in an app.

title: Oregon and Virginia sue SpaceX over Grok’s porn deepfakes
author: Jess Weatherbed
contentSnippet: In separate but similar lawsuits filed on Monday, Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield and Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones accused SpaceX of violating state consumer protection laws by ignoring industry-standard safeguards and falsely promoting the safety of its X social media platform and Grok AI features. The complaint filed in Virginia accuses Musk of willfully ignoring growing concerns around AI-generated sexualized deepfakes, and “instead saw a market opportunity for more profits,” describing the weak safeguards around Grok as “not a failure but a feature.” “Time and again, xAI and X told consumers they were being protected from abuses. That was false. Instead, the tool permitted users to routinely create and circulate non-consensual intimate imagery and sexualized images, and child sexual abuse material (CSAM), causing harm to individuals and children,” Jones said in a press statement. “Companies that deploy powerful tools don’t get to ignore consumer safety and call it innovation.” The complaints largely center around Grok Imagine, a tool that allows Grok and X users to generate images and videos. In August 2025, Grok maker xAI (which Musk has since merged with SpaceX) launched a “spicy” mode for Grok Imagine that spat out sexualized content including nude deepfakes of celebrities like Taylor Swift. In January 2026, Grok gained a feature that allowed X users to instantly edit any image without requiring consent from the original poster — resulting in X becoming flooded with nonconsensual, sexualized deepfakes of adults and minors. xAI made several changes to restrict access to Grok image editing, moving some capabilities behind a paywall and blocking certain requests for sexual poses, swimwear, or explicit scenarios. Our testing at the Verge following these restriction updates found they did little to prevent the bot from creating sexualized deepfakes, however. Both of the Oregon and Virginia lawsuits are seeking financial damages. The X Safety team said in a statement released after the lawsuits were announced that it takes appropriate measures to address users who generate sexual content involving minors: > “The people who tried to use Grok Imagine to generate this material did so by deliberately violating our Terms of Service and working aggressively to circumvent our safeguards. When some of these bad actors found ways to misuse Grok Imagine e

summary.tldr:
Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield and Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones filed separate lawsuits on Monday against SpaceX—which has merged with xAI—accusing the company of violating state consumer protection laws. The complaints allege that SpaceX and xAI falsely marketed the safety of the X platform and Grok AI features while willfully ignoring the proliferation of non-consensual intimate imagery, celebrity nude deepfakes, and child sexual abuse material (CSAM).

The legal actions focus on Grok Imagine, an image and video generation tool. In August 2025, xAI introduced a "spicy" mode that produced sexualized content, followed by a January 2026 feature allowing users to instantly edit any image without consent. Although xAI subsequently placed some capabilities behind a paywall and blocked specific prompts involving swimwear, explicit scenarios, or sexual poses, testing by reporters revealed that these restrictions failed to stop the generation of sexualized deepfakes.

Both state attorneys general are seeking financial damages. In response, the X Safety team issued a statement asserting that the platform utilizes prompt screening classifiers, output checks, and tightened protections to penalize bad actors who deliberately circumvent terms of service.
takeaways: **Plaintiff States:** Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield and Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones filed separate consumer protection lawsuits on Monday against SpaceX.

**Core Allegations:** The lawsuits accuse SpaceX and xAI of falsely promoting platform safety while willfully allowing the creation and circulation of non-consensual intimate imagery, celebrity nude deepfakes, and child sexual abuse material (CSAM).

**Product Timelines:** In August 2025, xAI launched a "spicy" mode for Grok Imagine, and in January 2026, the platform added an instant image-editing feature that did not require consent from original posters.

**Platform Countermeasures:** The X Safety team stated it deploys pre-prompt screening classifiers, post-output checks, and continuous protection adjustments to target users who violate terms of service.

title: AWS is making AI agents more decisive and secure with its latest Strands updates
author: Mike Wheatley
contentSnippet:
UPDATED 13:00 EST / NOVEMBER 23 2026

AWS is making AI agents more decisive and secure with its latest Strands updates

Amazon Web Services Inc. is trying to tackle two major headaches for artificial intelligence agents developers with a major update to Strands Agents, its open-source toolkit for building autonomous workers.

Today, the cloud infrastructure giant unveiled a new family of open-weight “decision models” called Strands Decider v2, along with the debut of Box CLI, bringing native sandbox support for popular coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Kiro CLI.

AWS introduced Strands Agents back in May 2025, and recently the project has emerged as the centerpiece of the company’s agentic development strategy. Strands Agents is a software development kit that gives developers a flexible, model-driven foundation for connecting large language models to enterprise data and tools.

After introducing Strands Harness , which allows Strands agents to be deployed in any computing environment, in September, AWS followed up with Strands Decider one month later. Unlike regular LLMs that focus on text outputs, Strands Decider is a category of decision models designed to evaluate scenarios and assign probability scores to a predetermined list of choices. At the time, AWS said decision models can help to improve the efficiency of AI agent workflows, such as routing support tickets or choosing which software tool to invoke to complete a given task.

More decisive agents

With Strands Decider v2, AWS is adding five even more capable decision models to its lineup. The open-weight models are built on Google LLC’s Gemma 4 architecture and they’re available in various sizes, ranging from a lightweight edge version to a beefy 31 billion-parameter variant for complex decision-making. In a blog post, AWS explained that the new models provide greater accuracy across text, image and video tasks, and deliver more optimal confidence scores, so agents can better determine when it’s OK to take an action or escalate to a human decision-maker.

The Strands Decider v2 models have also been given the ability to process longer inputs, including multistep agent execution logs, so they can collaborate with other agents.

title: Aevius Labs launches with $22M to bring understandable intelligence to medical data
author: Kyt Dotson
contentSnippet:
UPDATED 12:40 EST / NOVEMBER 23 2026

Aevius Labs launches with $22M to bring understandable intelligence to medical data

Boston-based Aevius Labs Inc. , a clinical medical data company, today announced it has raised $22 million in funding led by Insight Partners to build and train artificial intelligence foundation models that can understand and query unstructured medical text, imaging and other data.

A spinout of Mass General Brigham, a nonprofit academic healthcare system in Massachusetts, the company develops AI models that turn information from healthcare, payer, and life sciences organizations into insights other AI tools can act on. The company said it wants to provide a foundational “brain” that can take notes, medical artifacts, clinicians’ transcriptions, lab work, radiology imaging, electronic health record information and other specialty medical data, and make it more accessible to healthcare workers.

The platform can take all this information and use it to represent the whole patient, their medical experience, population studies and actionable insights for clinicians and doctors in the language that they speak. The company said it’s designed to support applications spanning healthcare delivery, operations, and life sciences.

The company was founded by key members of Modella AI Inc., which was acquired by pharmaceutical giant AstraZeneca PLC , using the company’s AI model and agent development for oncology research.

“Our mission is to make medicine computable,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Rowland Pettit, M.D., Ph.D. “As a physician-scientist, I’ve worked across many types of clinical data, and there is far more knowledge in those records than we’re able to use today.”

The company said its models learn relationships across different forms of medical data and throughout a patient’s history. It does this by building a dynamic, refreshable representation of the patient, essentially a computable picture of the patient and their entire medical clinical state and trajectory that the doctor or clinician can interact with. An organization can use this to build tools to forecast outcomes, identify changes and monitor outcomes over time.
